## Classification
Static measurement/API improvement, not a reproduced HTTP transport defect. Reviewed PR #1 at `572246a6e0b1a0eff5624e263c8880b7802446c9` (package version2026.10.29).

## Evidence
[`src/core.ts`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-http/blob/572246a6e0b1a0eff5624e263c8880b7802446c9/src/core.ts) defines `tokens(value)` as `ceil(max(JSON,TOON UTF-8 bytes)/4)`; `differencePacket` uses this for `estimatedTokens` and its budget. The receipt discloses the estimator, which is useful, but the SDK function comment calls it conservative and the PR description calls the measured output an “817-token” packet. [Real-data documentation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-http/blob/572246a6e0b1a0eff5624e263c8880b7802446c9/docs/real-data.md) labels these estimates rather than naming a tokenizer. UTF-8 bytes/4 is not a model token measurement or guaranteed upper bound.

Independent isolated source check on Node24.22.1 and SDK2026.10.28, using a synthetic injected read-only client (no HTTP requests, secrets or native mutation): one complete first-bad/last-good packet serializes to949JSON UTF-8 bytes and660TOON bytes including newline; reported `estimatedTokens=238` is exactly `ceil(949/4)`. No actual token count was measured.

## Impact / intended contract
The package's [canonical epic](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-http/blob/572246a6e0b1a0eff5624e263c8880b7802446c9/.agents/pm/epics/pm-http-76jn.toon) calls for bounded difference packets. Agent consumers need to distinguish an enforceable serialized-byte ceiling from approximate model cost, particularly with hashes, punctuation and different tokenizers. The proxy can remain an explicitly named estimate, but must not become proof that a model context budget fits or a measured token reduction. This proposal does not ask to weaken omissions, provenance or historical evidence.

## Acceptance / regression criteria
- Expose exact JSON and TOON UTF-8 bytes (including the final renderer/newline framing), with clearly documented byte-budget semantics or explicitly named heuristic units.
- If token budgets/counts are supported, name the tokenizer/model encoding and measure with it; otherwise avoid unqualified token counts and “conservative” model-token guarantees.
- Qualify the817 claim and body-only comparison; separately identify all successful-task commands, receipts and retries when presenting end-to-end cost.
- Keep self-inclusive receipt accounting, exact omitted/returned counts, restore instructions, complete-source distinction and all existing semantic oracles.
- Cover both renderers, long digests, non-ASCII strings and minimum receipt size. No paid model/API evaluation is necessary.

Limits: no tokenizer-specific undercount was measured here; this is an evidenced naming/measurement improvement, not a claim of a measured overflow or security failure. All-status issue scan found only PRs1–4 and no duplicate issue; native tracker record was checked.
Expose exact packet byte costs and distinguish heuristic units from tokenizer counts
